We need to propose a 5-step retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We need to output JSON tree with type mol root, children reaction nodes etc.

We need to find appropriate templates for each step. We have one template for deprotection of TBS (template_id 29646). That matches removal of TBS to give free OH. In target, there is no TBS; but we can consider a protecting group step in forward direction, so in retrosynthesis we would add TBS to protect an alcohol. So we need a step where we go from target to a protected intermediate (adding TBS). That is the reverse of deprotection: we need a template that adds TBS. The template we have is for deprotection (break O-Si, form OH). In retrosynthesis we apply that template forward (i.e., from protected to target). But we need reverse direction: we need to apply the template in reverse (i.e., we need a template that does protection). However we can still use the same template but in reverse direction: In retrosynthesis, we apply the template to break the bond that was formed in forward direction. The template we have is for forward deprotection (protected -> free OH). In retrosynthesis, we want to go from free OH (target) to protected (precursor). That is the reverse of the template, which is allowed if we treat the template as reversible? Usually retrosynthetic templates are given as reaction SMARTS for forward direction (reactants -> products). In retrosynthesis we need to apply the reverse direction (product -> reactants). The tool apply_template expects target molecule and template_id, and returns possible precursors (i.e., reverse application). So we can use template 29646 to get protected precursor.

Let's apply template 29646 to target to get protected precursor.
